item.cbc_more_content.small_bomb.tooltip: A compact _gravity bomb_ for precise drops. Can be combined into bundles of _up to four_ charges.
Releases from its mount. Keep the path in front of the nose clear.
Right-click to rotate; sneak and right-click to pick up.
Right-click a placed charge to enlarge its bundle.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.small_bom: Mount the bomb under a support: its nose follows the face you click.
A Create wrench rotates the charge. Leave an open drop corridor beneath it.
Power the mount to release the bomb. It separates and falls under gravity.
Impact detonates the charge. The centre takes the most damage; the rim is weaker.
Right-click a placed small bomb with more small bombs to build a bundle of up to four.
An explosion that destroys a stored charge can start a chain reaction. Separate storage from the release path.
item.cbc_more_content.small_bomb_2.toolt: A bundle containing _2 small bombs_. Releases one charge at a time; each produces _its own explosion_.
Releases all 2 charges in sequence. Removing power pauses the remaining bundle.
Sets the release interval for the connected rack: _6–100 ticks_.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.small_bom: This bundle holds exactly 2 small bombs in one mount.
Use the settings key on the mounted bundle to choose the spacing between releases.
The interval is 6–100 game ticks: 0.3–5 seconds at 20 TPS. It applies to the connected rack.
Keep power on: watch the bundle shrink after each of its 2 separate releases.
Remove power to pause before the next release. Restore it to use the remaining charges.
If another explosion destroys this bundle, it creates 2 delayed detonations. The release dial controls dropping, not this chain reaction.
item.cbc_more_content.small_bomb_3.toolt: A bundle containing _3 small bombs_. Releases one charge at a time; each produces _its own explosion_.
Releases all 3 charges in sequence. Removing power pauses the remaining bundle.
Sets the release interval for the connected rack: _6–100 ticks_.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.small_bom: This bundle holds exactly 3 small bombs in one mount.
Use the settings key on the mounted bundle to choose the spacing between releases.
The interval is 6–100 game ticks: 0.3–5 seconds at 20 TPS. It applies to the connected rack.
Keep power on: watch the bundle shrink after each of its 3 separate releases.
Remove power to pause before the next release. Restore it to use the remaining charges.
If another explosion destroys this bundle, it creates 3 delayed detonations. The release dial controls dropping, not this chain reaction.
item.cbc_more_content.small_bomb_4.toolt: A bundle containing _4 small bombs_. Releases one charge at a time; each produces _its own explosion_.
Releases all 4 charges in sequence. Removing power pauses the remaining bundle.
Sets the release interval for the connected rack: _6–100 ticks_.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.small_bom: This bundle holds exactly 4 small bombs in one mount.
Use the settings key on the mounted bundle to choose the spacing between releases.
The interval is 6–100 game ticks: 0.3–5 seconds at 20 TPS. It applies to the connected rack.
Keep power on: watch the bundle shrink after each of its 4 separate releases.
Remove power to pause before the next release. Restore it to use the remaining charges.
If another explosion destroys this bundle, it creates 4 delayed detonations. The release dial controls dropping, not this chain reaction.
item.cbc_more_content.medium_bomb.toolti: A _single falling charge_ with a wider blast than the small bomb. Useful when one compact crater is not enough.
Releases from its mount. Keep the path in front of the nose clear.
Right-click to rotate; sneak and right-click to pick up.
cbc_more_content.ponder.medium_bomb.head: Medium bomb: a wider impact
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.medium_bo: Install the medium bomb under a support, with room for the whole model and a clear drop path.
This is a single charge. Adding small bombs does not turn it into a cassette.
Supply redstone power to release it. The carrier keeps moving while the bomb falls.
Its broader blast damages terrain and physical ships caught within reach.
Damage weakens away from the centre. Surviving ground around the crater becomes disturbed soil.
Leave space between stored charges: a destroyed explosive can detonate in turn.
item.cbc_more_content.large_bomb.tooltip: A _heavy single bomb_ for a large impact area. Its blast also pushes physical constructions according to their mass.
Releases from its mount. Keep the path in front of the nose clear.
Right-click to rotate; sneak and right-click to pick up.
cbc_more_content.ponder.large_bomb.heade: Large bomb: release and blast footprint
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.large_bom: The large bomb needs an unobstructed mount. Aim its nose into the release corridor.
Use a wrench before launch to correct the orientation; sneak with the wrench to recover it.
Power releases one heavy charge. It is still a gravity bomb, not a guided missile.
The strongest destruction is near impact. The outer region is less destructive, with a disturbed soil border.
A physical hull can lose blocks and receive an impulse. A massive hull moves less than a light one.
Nearby explosive blocks can continue the blast as a chain reaction. Give the release area extra clearance.
item.cbc_more_content.moab.tooltip.summa: A _three-part heavy bomb_ with a broad crater and a pronounced centre. Occupies _three cells_ along its axis.
item.cbc_more_content.moab.tooltip.actio: Releases from its mount. Keep the path in front of the nose clear.
Right-click to rotate; sneak and right-click to pick up.
cbc_more_content.ponder.moab.header: MOAB: three-part mount and broad crater
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.moab_0: Clear three cells in a straight line for the nose, body and tail. The highlighted outline is the placement envelope.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.moab_1: Click the mounting face to point the nose outward. Sneaking uses your horizontal facing instead.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.moab_2: Use a wrench to rotate the complete bomb. All three destination cells must remain clear.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.moab_3: Redstone releases the entire MOAB as one charge; the tail is not a separate bomb.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.moab_4: The blast opens a broad, rounded crater with a deeper centre and a weaker outer rim. This scene is a reduced-scale illustration.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.moab_5: Physical ships within the blast can break and be pushed. Keep launch paths and ammunition storage apart.
item.cbc_more_content.sea_bomb.tooltip.s: A _water-running torpedo_. Outside water it follows a _falling arc_; after re-entry it resumes swimming.
item.cbc_more_content.sea_bomb.tooltip.a: Releases from its mount. Keep the path in front of the nose clear.
Right-click to rotate; sneak and right-click to pick up.
cbc_more_content.ponder.sea_bomb.header: Sea torpedo: water, air and re-entry
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.sea_bomb_: Install the torpedo in water with its nose aimed into an open channel. It can launch from a physical ship.
Redstone releases it from the mount. Leave enough space to clear the carrier's hull.
In water it travels forward. The blue section shows its underwater route.
After leaving water, gravity bends the trajectory downward. It cannot keep cruising through the air.
Re-entering water restores its water-running movement. A gap between pools does not freeze it in mid-air.
Impact detonates the torpedo against terrain or a hull. Water spray appears only when water is at or near the blast.
item.cbc_more_content.small_mine.tooltip: A low _contact mine_ triggered by living creatures stepping onto it. Can be buried in diggable ground.
Arms after _20 ticks_. Move away before it becomes active.
Right-click on diggable ground to bury it; sneak-click to uncover it.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.small_min: Place the small mine on solid, dry support. It can also be hidden on a bed.
There is a 20-tick arming delay: one second at normal tick rate. Step away promptly.
Use a shovel over soil, sand or other shovel-diggable ground to lower the mine into it.
Repeated clicks bury it further, up to eight steps. Sneak with the shovel to uncover it.
A living creature stepping on the armed mine triggers a ground-level explosion.
Burial conceals the model; it does not make the mine safe to walk over.
item.cbc_more_content.bounding_mine.tool: A _proximity mine_ that jumps before bursting. Notices living creatures slightly beyond its own cell.
Arms after _20 ticks_. Move away before it becomes active.
Right-click on diggable ground to bury it; sneak-click to uncover it.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.bounding_: Set the bounding mine on a dry support and leave during its 20-tick arming delay.
A shovel can hide it in suitable ground. Stone and planks cannot be dug into.
Its trigger reaches half a block beyond its cell. A nearby creature can trigger it without stepping on the centre.
The triggered charge leaves the ground and rises before it bursts.
The burst happens above the surface. Its main threat is to nearby creatures, including those behind low cover.
This differs from a heavy ground-blasting mine: do not judge its effect by crater size alone.
item.cbc_more_content.large_mine.tooltip: A broad _vehicle-contact mine_ for physical hulls and supported wheels. Ordinary footsteps are not its trigger.
Arms after _20 ticks_. Move away before it becomes active.
Right-click on diggable ground to bury it; sneak-click to uncover it.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.large_min: Place the antivehicle mine on the route of a physical hull or supported vehicle wheel.
It arms after 20 ticks. Its broad disc covers the cell so wheel contact can reach it.
Use a shovel to conceal the disc in diggable ground; uncover it with sneak-clicks.
Unlike the small mine, an ordinary living creature walking over it is not the vehicle trigger.
Contact from a Sable hull or a supported Offroad wheel triggers the charge.
The hull may lose blocks and receive an impulse. Greater mass reduces its movement from the same blast.
item.cbc_more_content.sea_mine.tooltip.s: A floating _contact charge_. Water ages it through _four states, 0–3_; corrosion increases the chance of a contact misfire.
item.cbc_more_content.sea_mine.tooltip.a: Becomes a physical floating body. Each wet stage takes _36,000 game ticks_.
Misfire chances: _0 / 15 / 35 / 65%_. A dull knock means the collision failed to detonate it.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.sea_mine_: Place the mine in water. It assembles into its own floating physical body.
A hull, swimmer or boat contacting the active mine can trigger its charge.
Water exposure advances corrosion: 0, 1, 2, 3. These are four total states, including the new mine.
Each stage needs 36,000 wet game ticks: 30 minutes at 20 TPS. Dry time does not advance corrosion.
The contact misfire chance rises from 0% to 15%, 35% and 65%. A dull knock is a misfire, not a successful explosion.
A rusty mine is still dangerous: a later contact may work. Underwater detonation damages nearby hulls and produces water effects.
item.cbc_more_content.cruise_missile.too: A _guided three-part missile_. Select coordinate, remote or compatible radar guidance before launch.
Opens the target and guidance panel.
Save the target, then use _redstone_ to launch.
Pair a designator, acquire a target and use its attack control to fire.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.cruise_mi: Leave three clear cells for the missile and an open path beyond its nose.
Use the settings key to choose coordinates or remote guidance. The three animated diagrams select direct, climbing arc or weaving flight.
Direct flight saves fuel; the arc climbs before descending; weaving changes course and speed and burns fuel faster.
Save a fixed point and launch with redstone, or right-click with a designator to arm remote guidance immediately.
Designated targets must be at least 50 blocks from the launcher. The operator's own hull does not block aiming.
The impact blast resembles a weaker MOAB. Intercept mode instead needs a compatible Create Radar setup and a bound controller.
A _remote targeting tool_ for cruise missiles. Acquires _moving physical hulls_ through the operator’s own ship.
Arms _remote_ guidance and adds the missile to a group of up to _eight_.
Hold a marked hull for _40 ticks_ to lock; attack launches the linked group.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.target_de: Place two missiles with a clear launch path. The same designator can control a group of up to eight.
Right-click each missile with the designator. It switches to remote guidance and the action bar confirms the group size.
Moving physical hulls receive markers. The target must be at least 50 blocks from the launcher; the designator range is 220 blocks.
Keep the marker under the crosshair and hold use for 40 ticks. Changing targets restarts acquisition.
After confirmation, press attack once to launch the linked group. Binding alone does not fire the missiles.
Your own hull is ignored by aiming. Terrain and other hulls still obstruct it; a stopped or unloaded target loses its lock.
item.cbc_more_content.aim9.tooltip.summa: An _air-to-air interceptor_ for airborne cruise missiles. Cold-launches above its rack, ignites and _leads the moving target_.
item.cbc_more_content.aim9.tooltip.actio: Switch interception on, select cruise missiles and set a _40–220 block_ acquisition radius.
Needs three clear cells. Rotate the complete airframe or sneak-click to recover it. Enabled racks _launch automatically_.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.aim9_0: Place the three-part AIM-9 with clear space above it. Its first movement is an upward cold launch, even on a banked carrier.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.aim9_1: Right-click any segment with the settings key. Enable the system and switch cruise-missile interception on.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.aim9_2: The slider sets a spherical acquisition radius from 40 to 220 blocks. Outside that radius the interceptor stays on its rack.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.aim9_3: An airborne cruise missile enters the selected radius: the AIM-9 assigns itself that contact and launches automatically. Other racks keep their rounds while that target is assigned.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.aim9_4: First it rises on ejection gas. Then a sharp ignition pop lights its compact exhaust and acceleration builds smoothly. Guidance aims ahead of the moving target.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.aim9_5: The target-specific proximity fuse bursts close to the cruise missile. The interceptor is consumed; the intercepted warhead can still explode. After a lost contact, the AIM-9 extinguishes and disappears.
item.cbc_more_content.c4.tooltip.summary: A throwable _sticky charge_ with a code and a choice of _timed or remote_ detonation.
item.cbc_more_content.c4.tooltip.action1: Throws a short distance; sticks to the surface it hits.
item.cbc_more_content.c4.tooltip.action2: Set a _four-digit code_ and timer or remote mode. The same code disarms an active charge.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.c4_0: Use C4 to throw it a short distance. It sticks where it lands, including walls and ceilings.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.c4_1: Open the attached charge with the settings key. Choose a four-digit code you will remember.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.c4_2: Timer mode allows 5–45 seconds. Confirming the arming panel starts the countdown.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.c4_3: Remote mode arms the receiver without a countdown. Pair that waiting charge with a detonator.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.c4_4: To disarm, reopen with the settings key and enter the same code. Wire cutters offer a separate, uncertain wire puzzle.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.c4_5: Breaking an armed charge is not a safe substitute for disarming it. Deal with its fuse first.
A _remote control_ for up to _12 armed C4 charges_. Reaches loaded charges within _250 blocks_.
Adds the waiting charge. Sneak-click removes that charge from the group.
Fires reachable charges. Sneak-use clears the group, or toggles a link to a vest you are wearing.
cbc_more_content.ponder.detonator.header: Detonator: build and fire a charge group
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.detonator: Prepare C4 in remote mode with the settings key. A timed or idle charge cannot be paired this way.
Right-click the waiting charge with the detonator. Repeat on other charges to add up to twelve.
The tooltip lists paired positions. Sneak-click one charge to remove only that pairing.
Use the detonator in the air to fire the group. Charges must be loaded and within 250 blocks.
Out-of-range charges stay on the list. Move within range instead of assuming every charge has fired.
Sneak-use clears the group unless you are wearing a bomb vest: then it toggles the vest link instead.
A _wearable charge_ occupying the chest slot. A detonator must be linked while the vest is worn.
Equip the vest before attempting to pair it.
Toggles the link to your worn vest. Ordinary use activates a linked, still-worn vest.
cbc_more_content.ponder.bomb_vest.header: Bomb vest: equipment and remote link
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.bomb_vest: Equip the bomb vest in the chest slot. Holding it in the inventory is not the same as wearing it.
With the vest on, sneak and use a detonator in the air to create the link.
The item status and periodic ticking indicate the link. Check that status before relying on the control.
Using the linked detonator normally activates the vest on its wearer.
Sneak-use the detonator again while wearing the vest to unlink it.
Removing the vest prevents that worn-vest activation. Equipping it does not turn it into a thrown C4 charge.
item.cbc_more_content.wire_cutters.toolt: Cuts placed _tripwires_ or opens the wire panel of _active C4_. Wire colours do not guarantee a safe choice.
Removes the attached tripwire without its trigger pulse.
Opens three wires: one disarms, one detonates, one accelerates. Roles are randomized.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.wire_cutt: For a tripwire, right-click either anchor block with the cutters.
The wire is removed without the crossing signal. The spent wire does not return a coil.
For C4, use the cutters on an armed charge to open its wire panel.
The three wire roles are randomized when armed: defuse, immediate detonation, or a shorter remaining fuse.
Colours are not a reusable solution. Closing and reopening the panel does not reset cuts or reroll this charge.
If you know the arming code, the settings key provides the direct code-based disarming route.
item.cbc_more_content.tripwire_coil.tool: A _one-use crossing sensor_ between two solid anchors, at most _8 blocks_ apart. Sends redstone to both ends.
Select the first, then the second. One anchor cannot hold two tripwires.
Cancels an unfinished selection. Cut a completed wire with wire cutters.
cbc_more_content.ponder.tripwire_coil.he: Tripwire: two anchors and one crossing
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.tripwire_: Choose two solid, dry anchor blocks. Fluids and replaceable blocks cannot hold this wire.
Right-click the first anchor with the coil, then the second. The direct distance must not exceed eight blocks.
The line follows its anchors on Sable sublevels too. Each anchor can carry only one tripwire.
Crossing the line parts it and sends a pulse to both anchors. Merely touching and backing away is different from crossing.
Connect a redstone-controlled device near an anchor. The wire itself contains no explosive charge.
The wire is spent after triggering. Cutters remove it without the crossing pulse; sneak-use cancels a first-end selection.
item.cbc_more_content.chain_coil.tooltip: A separate _chain connection_ using Simulated rope mechanics. Links compatible connectors and a winch while retaining the chain appearance.
Select the first endpoint, then the second. A connection uses one coil.
Cancels endpoint selection. Two winches cannot connect directly.
cbc_more_content.ponder.chain_coil.heade: Chain coil: connect a physical load
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.chain_coi: Place two compatible connection points: chain connectors, native rope connectors, or one winch and a connector.
Click the first endpoint with the chain coil. Move to the second while checking the preview.
Click the second endpoint to complete the chain. One coil is consumed for a valid connection.
The link uses Simulated's rope constraints: a physical load can move until the connection becomes taut.
A winch can operate the connection using its normal controls. Two winches cannot be linked directly to each other.
Sneak-click a block to cancel an unfinished endpoint selection. The ordinary rope item remains a separate item.
item.cbc_more_content.chain_connector.to: A _chain-only socket_ with Simulated connector behaviour. Can be _waterlogged_ without leaving an air pocket.
Select this socket as an endpoint. The ordinary rope coil cannot attach here.
Water occupies the space around the model. Attach it to the physical body you intend to restrain.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.chain_con: Mount the connector on the body you want to attach. The socket is an endpoint, not a chain by itself.
Use the Warnautics chain coil to select this socket, then choose a compatible second endpoint.
This socket accepts the chain coil only. A native rope coil is rejected here.
On a physical body, the attachment travels with that body while the connection limits its separation.
Place the socket underwater: water fills the block around the model, rather than leaving a dry cube.
Choose a winch as the other endpoint when adjustable length is needed. Its normal Simulated controls still apply.
item.cbc_more_content.siren.tooltip.summ: A _kinetic warning siren_. Requires rotation from below; sounds on a redstone signal or a configured threat detection.
item.cbc_more_content.siren.tooltip.acti: More speed increases volume; _64 RPM_ reaches full voice. Redstone alone cannot spin it.
Adjust automatic detection, radius, threat types and linger time.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.siren_0: Place the siren above a vertical shaft. Its mechanical input is underneath the stand.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.siren_1: Supply rotation. Volume rises with speed and reaches full strength at 64 RPM; a stalled rotor is silent.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.siren_2: A redstone signal requests sound while held. Without mechanical drive, that signal alone produces no voice.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.siren_3: Use the settings key to enable automatic detection and choose missiles, bombs, or both.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.siren_4: Detection radius is adjustable from 16 to 256 blocks. Linger keeps a detected-threat alarm sounding after the sighting.
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.siren_5: On a moving ship, sound follows the siren. If it is quiet, check shaft speed, network stress and the alarm settings.
item.cbc_more_content.settings_key.toolt: A _configuration tool_ for bomb racks, cruise missiles, sirens and C4. The clicked device determines the panel.
Opens its settings. Small-bomb intervals apply across the connected rack.
Click a radar device, then an intercept missile to bind it. Sneak-use in the air cancels binding mode.
cbc_more_content.ponder.settings_key.hea: Settings key: one tool, different panels
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.settings_: Right-click a small-bomb rack to open its release dial. The interval applies to the connected rack, not just the clicked bundle.
On a cruise missile, the same key opens target coordinates and guidance modes.
On a siren, configure detection radius, threat filters and alarm linger.
On C4, set an arming code and fuse mode; on active C4, enter its code to disarm.
With compatible Create Radar installed, click a radar device and then an intercept-mode missile to bind them.
While bound to a radar, the key has a different job. Sneak-use in the air returns it to ordinary settings; sneak-click a radar opens its intercept conditions.
item.cbc_more_content.music_disc_breaker: A _music disc_ for a jukebox. Plays _Breaker of Skies_ as background music for your builds.
Inserts the record and starts playback.
Ejects the record and stops playback.
cbc_more_content.ponder.music_disc_break: Breaker of Skies: playing the record
cbc_more_content.ponder.shared.music_dis: Place a jukebox where you want the music to play. This disc uses the normal record system.
Use Breaker of Skies on the empty jukebox to insert it.
The jukebox plays the track. Adjust the Jukebox/Note Blocks volume if the music is quiet.
A comparator can read the occupied jukebox, following normal Minecraft jukebox behaviour.
Use the jukebox again to eject the disc and stop playback. The record can be used again.
This is a record, not a siren mode: automatic threat warnings use the separate kinetic siren.

gui.cbc_more_content.aim9.title: AIM-9 / INTERCEPTOR
gui.cbc_more_content.aim9.hint: Auto-launch in range. One round per contact.
